seo.title: Homeless help in Philadelphia - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Philadelphia: shelter, meals, health care, benefits, work, identification, and legal support.

content.text: Immediate danger, police, fire, or ambulance:
Street outreach for a person living outdoors:
Food, shelter, benefits, and local referrals:

notice.text: Beds, meals, funding, routes, hours, and eligibility can change.

Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, benefit, housing, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.

content.text: Philadelphia has different shelter intake locations for families, single men, single women, veterans, and young adults. Tell staff your household members, age, gender identity, health or mobility needs, pregnancy, safety concerns, service animal or pet, and whether you need transportation. Ask for a backup plan if no bed is available.

during weekday daytime hours, visit Appletree Family Center or Roosevelt Darby Center for assessment. After hours, use the intake location matching your household below. For someone living outdoors, call Street Outreach at 215-232-1984. Placement depends on current capacity and assessment.
No Home Help is a volunteer-maintained directory, not an emergency service or service provider.

categories.title: 1. Urgent help, outreach, and severe weather

content.text: Call for immediate violence, fire, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark and describe the danger first.
City of Philadelphia — safety and emergencies

Call for a person living outdoors who may need shelter, transport, medical care, behavioral-health help, or treatment. Give the exact location, clothing description, observed condition, and immediate risks. Outreach cannot force help or guarantee a shelter bed.
Ask about shelter intake, homelessness prevention, family needs, or how to correct a problem with a city-funded homeless service. Funding and placement are not guaranteed.
City of Philadelphia — services for people experiencing homelessness
Ask for a meal, pantry, shelter, benefits, health care, rent help, utility help, or another local service. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and ask what is open today.
Use these lines for suicidal thoughts, an emotional crisis, or an urgent mental-health or substance-use concern. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger.
Philadelphia may activate Code Blue when precipitation and temperature or dangerous wind chill create a serious cold risk. During an activation, call Street Outreach at
Rules and locations can change with the weather. Do not wait for an official activation if a person is confused, very drowsy, shivering uncontrollably, or has pale or numb skin; call 911.
City of Philadelphia — Code Blue help

items.name: City shelter intake — what to expect

content.text: City intake staff assess safety, household composition, health, disability, veteran status, and possible alternatives to shelter. They may connect people to shelter, medical or behavioral-health care, treatment, child services, case management, or supportive housing. No assessment guarantees placement.

The city says a household should not be denied shelter entrance solely because it lacks identification, a birth certificate, or guardianship document. Bring papers if available, but do not delay an urgent request because they are missing.
City of Philadelphia — find emergency housing
Daytime shelter and diversion assessment. Explain every household member and any medical, disability, language, pregnancy, safety, or transportation need.
Daytime shelter and diversion assessment. Arrive as early as possible and ask for written directions to the next site if staff refer you elsewhere.

items.name: Red Shield Family Residence — families after hours

content.text: weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; holidays and weekends.
After-hours intake for families. Space is not guaranteed. Tell staff if anyone is a minor, pregnant, ill, disabled, fleeing violence, or without a safe place that night.
City of Philadelphia — after-hours family intake
weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; 24 hours on holidays and weekends.
Another after-hours family intake location. Call when possible to confirm where to go and ask about transportation if the household cannot reach the site safely.

items.name: Mike Hinson Resource Center — single men after hours

content.text: After-hours intake for single men. Ask what time to arrive, whether transport is available, and what to do if capacity is full.

items.name: Gaudenzia House of Passage — single women after hours

content.text: 111 N. 49th Street, entrance at 48th Street and Haverford Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19139
weekdays 5:00 p.m.–7:00 a.m.; holidays and weekends.
After-hours intake for single women. The city says people may use the center that most closely fits their gender identity.
City of Philadelphia — after-hours women's intake

Emergency shelter and support for young adults ages 18–24, including food, health, education, and career help. The provider states that services are inclusive of LGBTQ+ young people. Capacity and eligibility still apply.

items.name: Philadelphia Domestic Violence Hotline — confidential shelter

content.text: Safety planning, crisis support, interpretation, and possible emergency shelter for survivors and their children. Shelter addresses are confidential and space is limited. Call 911 for immediate danger.
Shelter and diversion assessment for veterans. If the office is closed or travel is impossible, call the national veteran line at
Use the city finder or call for the closest free meal or grocery site open today. Ask about the schedule, registration, identification, household limits, and whether food can be carried away.
City of Philadelphia — find free food or meals
The meal is open to all. Broad Street Love offers optional spiritual support but says it is not a practicing faith community. Its other services continue until 3:00 p.m.
. The provider publishes meals every day of the year, including Monday 4:30–6:00 p.m. and Friday–Sunday 11:30 a.m.–1:00 p.m.

The provider's current page formats some midweek morning times unclearly, so call before relying on Tuesday–Thursday hours. Toiletries, feminine products, diapers, and mail are also available on published schedules.
St. Francis Inn is a Catholic Franciscan ministry. Its services page does not state that worship is required.
St. Francis Inn — ministries and schedule
Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 6:00 p.m.; Saturday at 5:00 p.m.; Sunday at 9:30 a.m.
Chosen 300 is a Christian organization. Its Sunday page lists worship before the meal; the weekday schedule does not state that worship is a condition of eating. Confirm holiday changes.
Monday and Friday at 6:00 p.m.; Sunday at 9:00 a.m.
Schedules sometimes change for construction or holidays. Check the current provider notice before traveling.

items.name: The Center Philadelphia and Grace Café

content.text: Arch Street United Methodist Church, 55 N. Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19107
The daytime program includes a hot meal. Grace Café also publishes a Sunday to-go meal, generally 5:00–6:00 p.m. The church states that people are welcome regardless of spiritual tradition.

items.name: Old St. Joseph's Church — coffee and meal

content.text: Tuesday and Thursday, coffee at 10:30 a.m. and meal at 11:00 a.m.
This is a Catholic church. The city meal listing does not state that worship is required. Call before traveling because community-meal schedules can change.
City of Philadelphia — free meal locations
Meals and other basic-needs services are listed by the city and provider. Call for the current meal time and ask about health, legal, clothing, or social-service appointments available that day.

categories.title: 4. Day centers, showers, laundry, mail, and clothing

content.text: 1400 Arch Street, Sub Concourse; enter near the southeast corner of 15th Street and JFK Boulevard

Showers, laundry, clothing, coffee and meals, case management, shelter transport, medical care, behavioral-health care, medication treatment, and medication delivery. Weekday service times differ: the provider publishes last shower appointment at 3:15 p.m., last laundry appointment at 2:15 p.m., and shelter transport from noon to 4:00 p.m.
Dental service is closed until further notice. Arrive early because daily appointments can fill.

Mail, clothing, mending, personal-care services, meals, and a concierge desk for benefits, work, shelter, housing, and health referrals. New mailbox sign-up is published for Monday and Thursday, noon–2:00 p.m.
Provider pages list different days for some personal-care services, so ask the front desk for the current schedule.
Broad Street Love — frequently asked questions

Hot meal, showers, laundry, clothing, case management, computer access, and indoor relief. The program is hosted by Arch Street United Methodist Church and welcomes people regardless of religion or spiritual tradition.

Indoor respite, coffee, clothing, hygiene items, mail, case management, identification and benefits help, substance-use referrals, and shelter navigation. Prevention Point says its shelters do not accept walk-ins; use city intake for a bed request.
Day services for men, with meals, showers, clothing, mail, case management, and health connections. Call for the current public schedule before traveling.

categories.title: 5. Health, mental health, and substance-use help

content.text: 2144 Cecil B. Moore Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19121

Primary care, behavioral health, dental care, pharmacy, reproductive care, and child health. The center uses a sliding fee and states that care is available regardless of ability to pay. Walk-ins may be seen when a provider is available; appointments are safer.
Project HOME — Stephen Klein Wellness Center
Low-barrier medical care, behavioral-health support, medication treatment for opioid use, and medication delivery. Dental care is currently closed. Walk-in capacity can fill.
Project HOME — Hub of Hope health services
Connection to mental-health and substance-use treatment for Philadelphia Medicaid members and some uninsured residents. Ask for the nearest appropriate assessment or treatment provider.

items.name: Behavioral Health Special Initiative — uninsured residents

content.text: Assessment and connection to substance-use treatment for eligible uninsured or underinsured Philadelphia residents. Treatment depends on clinical assessment, eligibility, and current capacity.
Low-barrier substance-use assessment and connection to treatment, including medication for opioid-use disorder when clinically appropriate. Call 911 for overdose or immediate medical danger.
City of Philadelphia — harm-reduction and treatment resources
Virtual, low-barrier treatment support, including possible buprenorphine care. The city states that insurance is not required. Clinical decisions and prescriptions depend on assessment.
English and Spanish help finding substance-use treatment anywhere in Pennsylvania. Ask about transportation, medication treatment, detoxification, and payment options.
Pennsylvania Department of Drug and Alcohol Programs — Get Help Now

categories.title: 6. Benefits, housing, rent, and utility help

content.text: Free one-on-one help applying for food, health insurance, prescription, disability, utility, and other benefits. A counselor can help complete applications and follow up, but benefit agencies make the final decision.
Apply online for SNAP food benefits, Medical Assistance, cash assistance, LIHEAP energy help, and other state programs. Save the confirmation number and copies or photos of uploaded documents.
Online approval is not immediate. BenePhilly or a day center can help if you lack internet, an address, identification, or supporting records.

Information about possible help with rent, move-in costs, utilities, mediation, or emergency travel. Programs depend on eligibility and available funding; the recording or referral does not promise payment.

Call immediately after receiving a rent demand, termination notice, court complaint, lockout threat, or sheriff notice. Free legal advice or representation may be available depending on the case and capacity.
City of Philadelphia — free eviction legal help
The city provides some qualifying residents with free SEPTA travel, but there is no public application. Participants are selected through benefit records or designated community organizations.
Do not pay anyone to apply. Ask a benefit counselor whether another reduced-fare, disability, or senior transit program fits your situation.
City of Philadelphia — Zero Fare questions
Monday–Thursday 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Friday and Saturday 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Sunday closed.
Public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, scanning, charging outlets, restrooms, and accessible facilities. Ask staff what can be used without a library card or fixed address. Holiday hours can differ.
Free Library of Philadelphia — Parkway Central
Library social workers can help navigate shelter, benefits, identification, health, and other services. Availability may change, so ask at the information desk.
Transport may be available after shelter coordination. It is not a general free ride and does not guarantee placement. Arrive early and ask what backup route to use.
Ask BenePhilly or a library social worker about current federal Lifeline providers and eligibility. Never give a representative an original identity document or pay for a benefit application.
Job search, career counseling, workshops, hiring events, training referrals, unemployment navigation, and employer connections. Services and training funding do not guarantee employment.
Central-city employment center. Ask about computer access, résumés, identification barriers, training, and employers currently interviewing.
Employment and training assistance. Bring identification and a résumé if available, but ask staff what services can begin when documents are missing.
Job search and training support. Ask about same-day workshops, computer access, and employers open to applicants with gaps, limited experience, or a record.
Ask the concierge desk for help connecting to work, benefits, identification, health, shelter, or housing resources. It is a navigation service, not a job placement guarantee.

items.name: Free Pennsylvania photo ID for people experiencing homelessness

content.text: Pennsylvania waives the initial or renewal photo-ID fee for a person experiencing homelessness. A PennDOT Driver License Center uses Form DL-54A and may require identity and residency confirmation from a shelter or service provider.
Rules differ for replacement cards, driver-license reinstatement, or missing underlying documents. Ask Homeless Advocacy Project for help before paying anyone.
Free civil legal help for people experiencing or facing homelessness, including identification documents, public benefits, family matters, and access to records. Eligibility and capacity apply.
Ask what name, identification, and collection rules apply before using the address on benefit, court, employer, or health forms.

items.name: Prevention Point — mail, ID, and benefits navigation

content.text: Ask the Drop-In Center about receiving mail, replacing identification, benefits applications, and document storage practices. Availability may depend on enrollment and staff capacity.

Free civil legal help for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Ask about identification, SSI or SSDI, other benefits, family issues, records, or housing. The program cannot accept every case.

items.name: Weekly HAP clinic at Broad Street Love

content.text: Walk-in legal clinic through the Homeless Advocacy Project. Arrive early with every notice, court paper, benefit letter, identification record, and deadline. Clinic capacity can fill.

Legal information and possible representation for tenants facing eviction. Call as soon as a notice arrives; do not miss a hearing while waiting for a return call. Keep the lease, notices, payment proof, messages, photos, and court papers.
City of Philadelphia — eviction legal help

items.name: Protection from Abuse order — weekday filing

content.text: Family Court, 1501 Arch Street, 8th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19102

A Protection from Abuse order can address safety from an intimate partner or family member. Filing has no fee. Call the domestic-violence hotline for confidential planning and 911 for immediate danger.
Philadelphia Police — victim resources and PFA information

items.name: Emergency Protection from Abuse order — nights and weekends

content.text: Criminal Justice Center, 1301 Filbert Street, Room B-26, Philadelphia, PA 19107
Emergency after-hours PFA filing. Ask the domestic-violence hotline how to reach the correct entrance and make a safe plan for travel.

categories.title: 11. Domestic violence, sexual violence, and gender-specific help

content.text: Safety planning, crisis counseling, interpretation, and access to emergency shelter or other services for survivors and their children. The hotline serves people of any gender. Shelter space is not guaranteed.
Free legal help may be available for Protection from Abuse orders, custody, and support matters connected to domestic violence. Begin with the 24-hour hotline at

items.name: WOAR Philadelphia Center Against Sexual Violence

content.text: Confidential crisis counseling and support after sexual assault or abuse. Call 911 for immediate danger. A survivor can ask about medical care, evidence collection, reporting choices, accompaniment, and counseling without being forced to make every decision at once.
WOAR Philadelphia Center Against Sexual Violence

items.name: Gender identity at city shelter intake

content.text: The city states that a person is welcome to use the intake center that most closely fits their gender identity. Tell staff privately about safety, medication, mobility, or accommodation needs and ask for a supervisor if a problem occurs.
City of Philadelphia — emergency housing access

items.name: Covenant House — LGBTQ+ inclusive youth shelter

content.text: The provider states that its services for ages 18–24 are inclusive of LGBTQ+ young people. Ask about current shelter capacity, safety, health care, identification, education, and work support.

categories.title: 12. Families, youth, older adults, and disability needs

content.text: Use Appletree Family Center or Roosevelt Darby Center on weekday daytime hours. After hours, use Red Shield Family Residence or ACTS. Tell staff every child's age, school, medications, disability needs, pregnancy, and safety concern.
Do not delay urgent intake because identification, birth certificates, or guardianship papers are missing. Bring any documents you have.
City of Philadelphia — family emergency housing
2321 N. Broad Street and 5901 Market Street, Philadelphia
Youth access points for housing assessment and connections. Call to confirm which location to use and what services are available that day.
City of Philadelphia — youth access points

items.name: Synergy Project at Valley Youth House — ages 14–24

content.text: Monday–Thursday 8:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; Friday 8:30 a.m.–3:00 p.m.
Hygiene, showers, clothing, food, housing assessment, education and job help, and mental-health referrals for young people. Call ahead if under 18 or seeking overnight shelter.

items.name: School rights for students experiencing homelessness

content.text: Children and youth without stable housing have a right to free public education and may be able to enroll immediately even when residency or school records are missing. Ask the school counselor for the district's McKinney-Vento liaison and discuss school-of-origin options.
School District of Philadelphia — student rights

items.name: Philadelphia Corporation for Aging — age 60 and older

content.text: Service navigation for adults age 60 and older, including meals, care, housing-related support, and emergency needs. For suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, or serious self-neglect, choose option 1; that response is available 24 hours.
Philadelphia Corporation for Aging — help and questions

Tell intake staff about wheelchairs, oxygen, medications needing refrigeration, communication needs, a recent hospital discharge, pregnancy, or a trained service animal. Ask which site can safely meet the need and whether transportation is available.
Call 911 for a life-threatening medical condition. For non-emergency care, contact Stephen Klein Wellness Center at

items.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

content.text: Connection to VA homelessness programs, health care, housing, benefits, and local services. Veterans and people calling on a veteran's behalf may use the line. A referral does not guarantee immediate housing.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — call center

items.name: Philadelphia VA Community Resource and Referral Center

content.text: Monday–Friday, 8:00–11:30 a.m. and 1:00–3:00 p.m. Housing, health, mental-health, career, and benefit connections for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
VA — Community Resource and Referral Centers
Ask about emergency shelter assessment, housing, employment, benefits, and supportive services. Bring military records if available, but call even if documents are missing.

Philadelphia residents can request pet food, supplies, affordable veterinary care, transport, or temporary safety-net foster care for cats and dogs. Foster capacity is limited and PAWS cannot accept every request.
Links to pet food, low-cost veterinary care, Safe Havens for Pets, temporary foster care, and limited short-term boarding. Each program has its own eligibility, capacity, and reclaim rules.
Do not abandon or surrender an animal based only on an online listing. Contact the program and make a confirmed plan first.
ACCT Philly — help keeping a pet

Tell shelter intake staff that you have a trained service animal and describe the disability-related tasks it performs. Pets and emotional-support animals may be handled under different rules, so ask before traveling and request a supervisor if an accommodation problem occurs.
For a pet that is not a trained service animal, contact PAWS or ACCT before surrendering it. No temporary-care option is guaranteed.
U.S. Department of Justice — service-animal rights

items.text: If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911. For a mental-health or substance-use crisis without immediate physical danger, call or text 988.
For someone living outdoors, call 215-232-1984. For a shelter request, use daytime city intake or the after-hours location matching the household.
Ask intake for a backup plan, safe waiting place, and transportation if there is no bed. During severe cold, ask whether Code Blue is active.
For food, showers, laundry, mail, and health care today, check Hub of Hope, Broad Street Love, The Center Philadelphia, or Prevention Point. Arrive early.
Use BenePhilly for benefits, PA CareerLink for work, Homeless Advocacy Project for identification or civil legal help, and the tenant hotline for eviction.
Write down each program, the person you spoke with, time, next step, and documents requested. Photograph papers when possible and keep every court or benefit deadline.

content.text: If a listing is wrong or has changed:
use the contribution link below and include the provider's official source. Do not publish a survivor's confidential address or anyone's personal information.
